meta.program_name: Project Horizon — SAP S/4HANA & SAP Ariba Implementation
meta.solution_scope: SAP Ariba Guided Buying, Buying & Invoicing, Sourcing, Contracts and SLP, integrated with S/4HANA MM. Wave 1: UK and PL entities. DE entity deferred to Wave 2.

source_documents.title: Procurement Operations — as-is buying, sourcing and contracts
source_documents.author_or_participants: Head of Procurement Ops; 2 × Senior Buyer; Buying Team Lead (EMEA)

source_documents.title: Business Requisitioners & Budget Approvers workshop (22 attendees)
source_documents.author_or_participants: Engineering, Marketing, Facilities, IT, R&D representatives

source_documents.title: PH-FS-014 v1.6 — Guided Buying & Approval Framework
PH-FS-021 v1.2 — Supplier Enablement & Invoice Automation

impacts.as_is_process: Requisitioner emails a free-form request to the shared procurement mailbox and waits. No standard form, no status visibility; chasing by email is the norm. Around a third of requests are returned for missing cost centre or specification.
impacts.to_be_process: Requisitioner self-serves in Guided Buying: picks a category tile, buys from a catalogue or completes a structured non-catalogue form, and tracks status themselves. Cost centre, GL, delivery site and required-by date are mandatory at entry — the request cannot be submitted incomplete.
impacts.impacted_roles: All employees with buying need; majority raise fewer than 10 requests per year
impacts.rating_override_reason: Scores to High (3.35), but this lands on 3,620 occasional users on day one and is the single most visible change in the programme. Response tier raised to Critical on volume and visibility, not on per-person magnitude.
impacts.impact_rationale: Buying shifts from 'email procurement and hope' (INT-02) to self-service with mandatory data entry at source (FS-01 §2.2). The user does more work up front in exchange for speed and visibility. Occasional users are the hard case: an R&D attendee put it as 'don't send me on a course in October for something I'll use in March' (INT-02).
impacts.benefit_narrative: You can see exactly where your order is without chasing anyone, and most orders approve within a day instead of taking 12–18.
impacts.training_timing: T-2 weeks, reinforced by in-app guidance at point of use
impacts.key_message: You'll raise requests yourself in a guided shopping-style tool instead of emailing Procurement — and for the first time you'll be able to see where your order is.
impacts.comms_channel: Town hall; line-manager cascade; intranet; in-app announcement; short demo video
impacts.comms_owner: Chief Operating Officer (awareness); line managers (personal impact)
impacts.mitigation_actions: Do not rely on scheduled training for this group — they will have forgotten it by their next transaction. Point-of-use in-app guidance plus a one-page job aid is the primary channel; the course is secondary.
impacts.notes: Headcount figure excludes the DE entity (Wave 2). Confirm final Wave 1 population against the go-live scope — INT-02 flagged this as unresolved.

impacts.as_is_process: High-frequency requisitioners (Facilities, IT) email several requests per week and maintain informal relationships with named buyers to expedite. Urgent items handled by 'a phone call and a favour'.
impacts.as_is_system: Email / shared mailbox; direct buyer contact
impacts.to_be_process: Same Guided Buying flow as all requisitioners, but used daily. These users will hit catalogue rules, non-catalogue thresholds and the triage queue routinely and become the de-facto super-users in their functions.
impacts.impacted_roles: Facilities coordinators, IT asset and service coordinators
impacts.impact_rationale: Same process change as CI-001 but at high frequency, so the policy constraints bite daily rather than occasionally. This group also loses the informal expediting route through named buyers (INT-02), which is how urgent work gets done today.
impacts.benefit_narrative: No more chasing procurement for status — you raise, track and receipt your own orders, and repeat buys take minutes.
impacts.training_timing: T-3 weeks, plus super-user session at T-5 weeks
impacts.key_message: You'll do more of your own buying end to end — and the informal 'call a buyer' route is replaced by rules you can see and plan around.
impacts.comms_channel: Targeted email; super-user briefing; drop-in sessions
impacts.comms_owner: Head of Facilities; Head of IT Operations
impacts.mitigation_actions: Recruit 8–10 of this group as change champions ahead of go-live — they are the highest-volume users and will set the tone for their functions.

impacts.as_is_process: Everything is bought free-text. Requisitioners describe what they want in their own words and Procurement sources it. No restriction on what can be requested or from whom.
impacts.to_be_process: Buying channel is fixed by category: catalogue mandatory for IT Hardware, Stationery and MRO; structured non-catalogue form permitted for Engineering Services, R&D Consumables and Facilities Works; anything over €100k must go through a sourcing event. There is no free-text 'other' option.
impacts.impacted_roles: Engineers, R&D scientists and technical leads specifying bespoke goods and services
impacts.impact_rationale: This is a control change dressed as a system change, and this group has already said so. Engineering pushed back directly in the workshop: 'Half of what I buy is bespoke. If the system won't let me describe what I actually need, I'll go around it' (INT-02). FS-01 §2.3 confirms free-text purchasing is not available and unmatched requests route to a 2-day triage queue.
impacts.benefit_narrative: Catalogue items arrive faster and at pre-negotiated prices; the non-catalogue form still exists for genuinely bespoke work in your categories.
impacts.key_message: Bespoke technical buying still has a route — the non-catalogue form is open for Engineering Services and R&D Consumables. What changes is that it's a structured form, not an email.
impacts.comms_channel: Function-specific briefing; drop-in Q&A with the category leads; FAQ
impacts.mitigation_actions: Run a category-channel review workshop with Engineering and R&D before design freeze. The stated intent to 'go around it' is a live workaround risk — the fastest way to close it is to let this group test the non-catalogue form against real recent requisitions and adjust the category rules where it genuinely does not fit.
impacts.notes: Highest workaround risk in the register. Track adoption of the non-catalogue form vs. triage-queue volume in the first 8 weeks post go-live as the early warning signal.

impacts.as_is_process: Buyer looks up the approver on a SharePoint DOA spreadsheet last properly updated around 18 months ago, then emails them. Approver replies 'approved' by email, usually without line-item detail; the buyer files the email as evidence. Approvers routinely approve items above their actual authority.
impacts.to_be_process: Approval routes automatically from a DOA mastered off the HR org structure. Approver receives a task with full line-item detail and can approve, reject or return for edit only. They cannot approve above their limit, cannot edit line values, and cannot self-approve. Unactioned tasks escalate to their line manager after 3 working days.
impacts.impacted_roles: Cost centre owners, department heads, category approvers, Finance Director
impacts.impact_rationale: The workshop read this as a small change — most assumed enforced limits were already in place (INT-02). They are not. FS-01 §3.3 removes the override path entirely, and nobody in the room could state their own limit correctly. The gap between what this group believes and what the system will do is the actual risk here, and it will surface as a spike in rejected approvals in week one.
impacts.benefit_narrative: You'll see what you're actually approving, on your phone, and you'll stop being asked to sign off things that were never yours to sign.
impacts.key_message: Approvals move to your Ariba inbox with full detail — and the system will hold you to your actual limit, which may be lower than what you've been approving.
impacts.comms_channel: Targeted email with personalised DOA limit; line-manager cascade; FAQ
impacts.mitigation_actions: Send every approver their personal DOA limit in writing at T-4 weeks. Do not let go-live be the moment someone discovers their limit changed.

impacts.as_is_process: No aggregation. Purchases can be split across multiple requests to stay under an approval limit; this happens openly and is not treated as a control breach.
impacts.to_be_process: The system aggregates requests from the same requester, cost centre and supplier over a rolling 30 days and routes to the next approval tier once the aggregate crosses a threshold. The split-purchase route closes.
impacts.impacted_roles: Cost centre owners and budget holders who currently manage spend around approval thresholds
impacts.impact_rationale: Low mechanical impact, high behavioural impact. A Marketing attendee described splitting purchases to stay under their limit openly in the workshop, with no apparent awareness it was a control issue (INT-02). The control is new (SIG-01, FS-01 §3.4); the behaviour it closes is established and considered normal.
impacts.benefit_narrative: Fewer surprises at year end — committed spend is visible against your budget in real time rather than arriving as a monthly report.
impacts.key_message: Repeat purchases to the same supplier now add up against your limit over 30 days — plan the whole spend up front rather than in instalments.
impacts.comms_channel: Targeted email; finance business partner 1:1s
impacts.mitigation_actions: Frame this as a policy that already existed rather than a new restriction, and have Finance Business Partners raise it in existing 1:1s rather than in a broadcast. A public announcement invites the affected group to defend current practice; a private conversation does not.

impacts.as_is_process: The AP team performs goods receipt centrally from delivery paperwork. Requisitioners do nothing after their order is placed.
impacts.to_be_process: The named delivery contact on the requisition — by default the requisitioner — confirms receipt in Guided Buying or the mobile app. No invoice is paid without a receipt.
impacts.impacted_roles: All requisitioners and named delivery contacts
impacts.impact_rationale: This is net-new work moving from a central team to several thousand individuals (SIG-01 PH-P2P-040, FS-01 §4). Each instance is small, but it is an addition to the day job that nobody has asked for and that most requisitioners do not currently know is coming. Non-receipt directly blocks supplier payment, so low compliance here becomes an AP and supplier-relations problem within weeks.
impacts.benefit_narrative: Confirming receipt takes seconds on your phone and it's what gets your supplier paid on time — which is what stops them chasing you.
impacts.key_message: When your order arrives, confirm it in the app. It takes seconds, and it's the step that gets your supplier paid.
impacts.comms_channel: In-app prompt; job aid; line-manager cascade; automated reminder on overdue receipts
impacts.mitigation_actions: Instrument this from day one: track overdue receipts by cost centre weekly and route the list to line managers, not to individuals. This is the impact most likely to quietly fail, and the only reliable early signal is the ageing report.
impacts.dependencies: CI-011 (AP exception handling depends on receipt compliance)

impacts.as_is_process: Buyers receive ~900 email requisitions a month, chase missing data on about a third, manually key them into ECC, look up approvers on the SharePoint DOA, chase approvals, create the PO and email it to the supplier as a PDF. Buyers hold pricing knowledge personally — 'my price list is in my head and in a spreadsheet on my desktop'.
impacts.as_is_system: Email; SAP ECC (ME51N, ME21N); personal spreadsheets
impacts.to_be_process: Catalogue and approved non-catalogue orders create and transmit automatically with no buyer involvement. Buyer intervention is retained only for non-catalogue requests above €50k and exception-flagged requests. The role shifts from transaction processing to category support, exception handling and supplier performance.
impacts.to_be_system: SAP Ariba Buying & Invoicing / Ariba Network
impacts.impacted_roles: 14 Buyers, 3 Buying Team Leads
impacts.impact_rationale: The largest role change in the programme. The majority of what this team does daily is automated away (SIG-01 PH-P2P-030). The team knows it: 'So the system decides the price now? What am I for?' was raised twice, unprompted, by different Senior Buyers (INT-01). Personal pricing knowledge held in individual spreadsheets also becomes catalogue and contract data, which is a loss of individual standing as well as of task.
impacts.benefit_narrative: You stop keying other people's requisitions and start doing the category and supplier work you were hired for — but this only lands if the new role is described concretely and soon.
impacts.training_timing: T-5 weeks, plus floorwalking T-0 to T+4
impacts.key_message: Transactional buying is being automated. Your role moves to category support, exceptions and supplier performance — here is what that looks like, in writing, before go-live.
impacts.comms_channel: Team session with the Procurement Director; 1:1s with each buyer; written role description
impacts.comms_owner: Procurement Director (with each buyer's own line manager for the 1:1s)
impacts.mitigation_actions: Issue written to-be role descriptions before the first training session — asking this team to learn a system that removes their current job, without telling them what the new job is, will read as an answer to the 'what am I for' question that nobody intends. Team Lead (EMEA) has been through a failed ERP rollout ('two days of training six weeks before go-live, then nothing') and is the credibility test for this workstream: engage directly rather than through the cascade.
impacts.notes: PL team (4 buyers) flagged that all previous-programme training was English-only and delivered UK-time (INT-01). Confirm localisation and scheduling for the PL cohort before the training calendar is published.

impacts.as_is_process: Supplier receives a PDF purchase order by email from a named buyer and confirms informally by reply. Order queries go to the buyer directly.
impacts.to_be_process: Supplier receives the PO through the Ariba Network and confirms the order in the Network. Order status, changes and confirmations are transacted in the Network rather than by email with a named individual.
impacts.impacted_roles: Supplier sales, order management and account teams
impacts.impact_rationale: An external audience adopting a new transactional platform they do not control, on the client's timetable (FS-02 §1.1). They also lose the named-buyer relationship as the route for order queries. Supplier non-adoption is a leading cause of benefit shortfall on Ariba implementations, and this group carries ~90% of spend.
impacts.benefit_narrative: Orders arrive in a single channel with confirmed detail, and you can see PO and payment status yourself instead of emailing for it.
impacts.training_timing: T-10 to T-8 weeks, repeated across time zones
impacts.key_message: From January, Meridian orders come to you through the Ariba Network. Register now — suppliers who aren't enabled can't receive orders.
impacts.comms_channel: Supplier letter from the Procurement Director; enablement webinars; supplier portal; account-manager calls for the top 50
impacts.mitigation_actions: Named-contact enablement calls for the top 50 suppliers by spend rather than broadcast-only. Track enablement completion weekly against the T-10 target and escalate laggards to their Category Manager — this is a schedule risk, not a comms risk, once it slips.

impacts.as_is_process: Supplier is set up by the client's Master Data team from information supplied by email. The supplier does nothing beyond sending their details once.
impacts.to_be_process: Supplier self-registers on the Ariba Network and completes a qualification questionnaire covering financial, compliance, ESG and information security criteria. They then maintain their own contact, bank, tax and certification data on an ongoing basis. Suppliers not registered cannot be transacted with.
impacts.impacted_roles: Small supplier owners, office managers, finance contacts
impacts.impact_rationale: Registration is mandatory to keep trading (FS-02 §1.1) but this group represents only ~10% of spend, so the client has little relationship leverage and the supplier has little commercial incentive to invest effort. Tranche 3 (~400 suppliers) is self-service with no assigned owner (FS-02 §4). The realistic failure mode is not resistance but silence, discovered at go-live when a PO cannot be raised.
impacts.benefit_narrative: One free account, one place to see orders and payment status, and no more chasing us for remittance information.
impacts.key_message: Register on the Ariba Network before January or we won't be able to raise orders to you. It's free and takes about 20 minutes.
impacts.comms_channel: Supplier letter; step-by-step registration guide; supplier helpdesk; reminder sequence at T-8, T-6, T-4, T-2
impacts.mitigation_actions: Assign an owner for tranche 3 self-service enablement — FS-02 §4 records this as unassigned and it will not resolve itself. Agree the fallback position for non-enabled tail suppliers after T+8 weeks before go-live, not after: the decision (block, extend, or offboard) has commercial consequences that need Procurement Director sign-off.
impacts.notes: Tranche 3 population (~400) is an estimate from the spend analysis, not a validated list. Confirm against the vendor master before the enablement campaign is sized.

impacts.as_is_process: Supplier records are created and amended centrally from emailed information. Ownership of supplier master data is genuinely unclear — Finance believes Procurement owns it and Procurement believes Finance does.
impacts.to_be_process: Suppliers maintain their own contact, bank, tax, insurance and certification data. The Master Data team moves from creating records to reviewing and approving supplier-submitted changes. Bank detail changes require dual approval by Compliance and Finance plus a call-back verification.
impacts.impacted_roles: Master data analysts; Compliance reviewer; Finance approver
impacts.impact_rationale: The team's core activity — record creation — is removed and replaced by a control and review function with a new fraud-prevention obligation attached (FS-02 §1.2). Small team, high per-person impact. The pre-existing ownership ambiguity flagged in INT-01 means there is currently no single accountable owner to design the new operating model with.
impacts.benefit_narrative: You stop rekeying supplier details from emails and take on the control role — reviewing and approving changes rather than typing them.
impacts.key_message: Suppliers will maintain their own data. Your role becomes reviewing and approving what they submit — including a new dual-approval control on bank details.
impacts.comms_channel: Team session; 1:1 with each analyst; written role description
impacts.mitigation_actions: Resolve supplier master data ownership between Finance and Procurement before designing the review workflow. Escalate to the Steering Committee — this is a decision, not an engagement problem, and the control cannot be operated without an accountable owner.
impacts.notes: OPEN QUESTION: who owns supplier master data today, and who will own the review-and-approve function at go-live? INT-01 records Finance and Procurement each believing it is the other. Needs a Steering Committee decision.

impacts.process_name: Invoice Entry, Matching and Exception Handling
impacts.as_is_process: AP keys every invoice from PDF or paper, matches manually against the PO, and performs goods receipt centrally from delivery paperwork. The team also handles ~400 supplier payment queries a month through a shared mailbox.
impacts.to_be_process: Suppliers submit invoices through the Ariba Network; three-way match runs automatically within tolerance. AP handles exceptions only — price and quantity mismatch, missing goods receipt, blocked supplier, duplicate, tax code failure. Suppliers self-serve payment status, and the shared mailbox is targeted for decommissioning at T+6 months.
impacts.to_be_system: SAP Ariba Buying & Invoicing / Ariba Network
impacts.impacted_roles: AP clerks (7 UK, 4 PL); AP Team Lead
impacts.impact_rationale: The design targets 85% touchless processing against a current baseline of 0%, and the business case assumes AP transactional effort falls by ~70% (FS-02 §2.2–2.3). The team's entire current workload is the thing being automated. The business case assumes redeployment rather than reduction, but FS-02 §2.3 records that this has not been confirmed to the team in writing — so from where they sit, the honest reading of the programme is that it removes 70% of their work with no stated consequence.
impacts.benefit_narrative: Only meaningful once the redeployment position is stated. Until then this group has been given a number and no answer.
impacts.training_timing: T-4 weeks, plus hypercare T-0 to T+4
impacts.key_message: Invoice matching is being automated and your role becomes exception management. Here is what the team looks like after go-live — including headcount.
impacts.comms_channel: Team session with the CFO; 1:1s; written statement of the redeployment position
impacts.comms_owner: Chief Financial Officer (position statement); AP Team Lead (day-to-day)
impacts.mitigation_actions: Get the redeployment position confirmed in writing and communicated before AP training begins. This is the single highest-risk item in the register: an 11-person team is being asked to build the system that removes most of their current work, while the answer to 'what happens to us' exists only as an untested assumption in a business case. Escalate to the CFO with a date.
impacts.dependencies: CI-006 (touchless matching depends on requisitioner receipt compliance), CI-012
impacts.notes: The 85% touchless target is conditional on CI-006 goods-receipt compliance across 3,620 occasional users. If receipting lags, AP exception volume rises rather than falls and the redeployment case weakens — flag this dependency to the Steering Committee explicitly.

impacts.as_is_process: Supplier emails a PDF invoice or posts paper to the AP shared mailbox, then chases payment status by email or phone.
impacts.to_be_process: Supplier submits invoices through the Ariba Network by PO-flip, cXML integration or Network-hosted entry. Paper and PDF-email invoicing is decommissioned for enabled suppliers at go-live. Payment status is self-served in the Network.
impacts.impacted_roles: Supplier accounts receivable and billing teams
impacts.impact_rationale: A hard cutover for an external audience: the existing invoicing channel is switched off at T+0 (FS-02 §2.1), so a supplier who has not adopted the new one simply stops being able to bill. Tolerance rules (±2% or €50 on price, 0% on quantity) also mean invoices that would previously have been resolved by a phone call to AP will now reject automatically.
impacts.benefit_narrative: Invoices matched automatically get paid without chasing, and you can see payment status yourself instead of emailing AP.
impacts.training_timing: T-6 weeks, repeated across time zones
impacts.key_message: From go-live we can only accept invoices through the Ariba Network — PDF and paper invoices will not be processed. Matched invoices get paid without chasing.
impacts.comms_channel: Supplier letter; enablement webinar; step-by-step invoicing guide; supplier helpdesk
impacts.mitigation_actions: Publish the match tolerances to suppliers before go-live so rejections are predictable rather than mysterious, and staff the supplier helpdesk for the first 6 weeks at above steady-state levels.

impacts.as_is_process: Category Manager emails suppliers individually, builds a comparison spreadsheet by hand and negotiates second rounds by phone. Bids are visible only to the Category Manager until they make a recommendation — a standing audit finding. Nothing but the final number is recorded.
impacts.to_be_process: Events are built from templates and published to all invited suppliers simultaneously. Bids are sealed and invisible to everyone, including the Category Manager, until the event closes. Comparison is auto-generated, scoring is entered against pre-declared weighted criteria, and the award rationale is recorded in-system as the audit trail. Second-round negotiation runs as a further in-system round; offline negotiation is not supported. All spend above €100k must go through a competitive event.
impacts.impacted_roles: 8 Category Managers across 4 categories
impacts.impact_rationale: Every element of how this group works changes at once: the channel, the transparency model, the negotiation method and the mandate. Sealed bidding removes their privileged early sight of bid data, in-system scoring makes their judgement visible and challengeable, and the removal of offline negotiation takes away the tool they consider their core skill. The €100k mandate converts a policy expectation into an enforced control (SIG-02).
impacts.benefit_narrative: Award decisions become defensible — the audit finding on bid visibility closes, and the comparison work that eats your week is automated.
impacts.training_timing: T-6 weeks, plus a live pilot event at T-4
impacts.key_message: Sourcing moves in-system with sealed bids and recorded rationale. Negotiation doesn't disappear — it becomes a structured round with an audit trail behind it.
impacts.comms_channel: Team workshop with the Procurement Director; 1:1s; pilot event debrief
impacts.mitigation_actions: Run a real sourcing event in the system with this group before go-live rather than a training exercise — this is a small, expert, sceptical population and hands-on proof will move them further than any briefing. Involve them in designing the scoring criteria templates so the transparency is theirs rather than imposed.
impacts.notes: Category Managers were not represented in INT-01 (flagged in that session's open items). This row is built from the process design plus the Procurement Ops view of how sourcing works today — validate directly with the Category Manager group before baselining.

impacts.as_is_process: Contracts are Word documents emailed back and forth between the Category Manager and Legal. Version control is by filename convention. No structured record of which clauses deviate from standard.
impacts.to_be_process: Contracts are generated from an approved template against a clause library. Any deviation from a standard clause triggers a mandatory Legal review workflow. Version history and approval trail are held in the system.
impacts.impacted_roles: Commercial counsel and legal operations
impacts.impact_rationale: Legal moves from reviewing whole documents on request to reviewing flagged deviations in a workflow (SIG-02 PH-S2C-030). Volume of review should fall but the team loses discretion over what reaches them — the clause library decides. Building and maintaining that library is new work with no current owner.
impacts.benefit_narrative: You see the deviations rather than the whole document, and you stop being the version-control mechanism.
impacts.key_message: Contracts are drafted from a clause library and only deviations come to you — which means the library has to say what you would have said.
impacts.comms_channel: Team session; clause library design workshops
impacts.mitigation_actions: Legal must own the clause library content, not just review it. Schedule the library build as Legal-led work with programme support, and confirm the ongoing maintenance owner before go-live.
impacts.notes: No Legal stakeholder has been interviewed. This row is derived from the process design alone — schedule a Legal session before baselining.

impacts.as_is_process: Contracts sit in shared-drive folders by supplier name with no expiry tracking and no named owner. Lapses are discovered when a supplier calls about a PO that cannot be raised. Nobody has a definitive count of active contracts — around 400 is the working estimate.
impacts.to_be_process: Every contract is held in the repository with structured metadata and a named Contract Owner. The system issues automated expiry alerts at 180, 90 and 30 days to that owner, who is accountable for renewal or exit.
impacts.impacted_roles: Business managers who will be named as Contract Owner — role does not exist today
impacts.impact_rationale: SIG-02 PH-S2C-040 requires every contract to have a named Contract Owner. That role does not exist today, is not in anyone's objectives, and carries a real accountability — responding to expiry alerts and owning renewal or exit decisions. Named individuals will receive system alerts for a responsibility they have never been told they hold.
impacts.benefit_narrative: You stop finding out a contract lapsed from the supplier, and renewals become a planned conversation instead of an emergency.
impacts.training_timing: T-3 weeks — cannot precede role assignment
impacts.key_message: You've been named as owner of these contracts. Here's what that means, what the system will send you, and when.
impacts.comms_channel: Personal notification listing the individual's assigned contracts; line-manager briefing; job aid
impacts.mitigation_actions: Assign and confirm Contract Owners with their line managers before go-live, and get the accountability into objectives. An unassigned or unaware owner means the expiry alert goes nowhere and the programme has replaced one silent failure mode with another.
impacts.notes: OPEN QUESTION: the ~60 headcount is extrapolated from the ~400 estimated active contracts at roughly 6–7 contracts per owner. Neither the contract count nor the owner population is confirmed — INT-01 records that nobody has a definitive contract count. Contract inventory and owner assignment both need to complete before this row can be sized or trained.

impacts.as_is_process: The Procurement Analyst manually builds a quarterly spend cube and issues it to Category Managers and Finance. This is the role's primary deliverable and the main basis of its standing in the function.
impacts.to_be_process: Spend analytics is delivered by the platform. Category Managers self-serve dashboards; cost centre owners see live committed spend. The manual quarterly cube is not produced.
impacts.impacted_roles: Procurement Analyst (single post holder)
impacts.impact_rationale: FS-02 §3 eliminates this role's primary deliverable and records that no revised role definition exists. A single post holder whose main output disappears, with nothing yet defined to replace it. Small population, maximum individual impact — and the kind of impact that is easy to miss in a register organised by stakeholder group size.
impacts.benefit_narrative: Cannot be stated credibly until the revised role is defined. Do not attempt a benefit message to this individual before that exists.
impacts.key_message: Handled 1:1 by the line manager, not by programme communication.
impacts.comms_channel: 1:1 with line manager; HR involvement as required
impacts.mitigation_actions: Define the revised role — or the alternative — before this individual hears about the change through a programme channel. A single-person impact of this severity is a line management and HR matter first and a change communication matter second.
impacts.notes: OPEN QUESTION: what is the revised role definition? FS-02 §3 records that none exists. Needs a Procurement Director decision with HR before any communication to the post holder.

impacts.as_is_process: Finance issues a monthly commitment report to cost centre owners. Business Partners field questions about it and reconcile discrepancies by hand.
impacts.to_be_process: Cost centre owners see live committed spend against budget in the system. The monthly commitment report is retired and Business Partners move to advising on the live data rather than producing and explaining a lagging report.
impacts.impacted_roles: Finance Business Partners supporting UK and PL cost centres
impacts.impact_rationale: A favourable change for this group — a manual monthly production task is replaced by live data (FS-01 §5). The adjustment is that their cost centre owners now see the same numbers they do, in real time, which changes the nature of the conversation more than the workload.
impacts.benefit_narrative: You stop building and defending a monthly report and start advising on numbers your stakeholders can already see.
impacts.key_message: The monthly commitment report is going away — your cost centre owners will see committed spend live, and your role shifts to advising on it.
impacts.comms_channel: Finance team briefing; e-learning

impacts.as_is_process: Urgent purchases are handled by phoning a known buyer, who raises the PO immediately and completes the paperwork afterwards. Described in the workshop as 'a phone call and a favour'.
impacts.to_be_process: Not designed. SIG-01 holds a placeholder task (PH-P2P-015) with no content and FS-01 §6 records the specification as deferred at design authority on 2026-05-14 with no target date and no owner beyond the workstream lead.
impacts.impacted_roles: Facilities, IT and Engineering staff handling breakdowns, outages and safety-critical purchases
impacts.impact_rationale: Scored on the assumption that the current informal route closes and is replaced by something more controlled — but the to-be does not exist. Attendees asked repeatedly how urgent purchases would work and no answer was available (INT-02). If nothing is designed, the practical outcome is that the informal route continues outside the system, which undermines the control model and the spend data at the same time.
impacts.benefit_narrative: Cannot be stated until the process exists.
impacts.training_timing: TBC — cannot be scheduled until the process is designed
impacts.key_message: TBC — this group has asked twice and been given no answer. Silence is itself a message here.
impacts.comms_channel: TBC
impacts.mitigation_actions: Escalate the undesigned emergency path to the Steering Committee as a go-live risk, not a design backlog item. Facilities and IT cannot be trained on a process that does not exist, and this is the group most likely to be raising a purchase at 2am on a Sunday.
impacts.notes: OPEN QUESTION: what is the emergency purchasing process? Deferred at design authority 2026-05-14 (FS-01 §6) with no target date. All scores on this row are provisional and assume a controlled replacement for the current informal route — re-score once the design exists.

impacts.as_is_process: Warehouse team receipts stock deliveries against the PO using the standard SAP warehouse transaction, working from the printed PO and the delivery note.
impacts.to_be_process: Unchanged in flow and system — the warehouse transaction and the receipting step stay as they are. What changes is that stock POs now originate in Ariba, so the PO number format and the document header look different, and the buyer named on the PO may no longer be a person.
impacts.impacted_roles: Goods-in operatives and warehouse supervisors
impacts.impact_rationale: SIG-01 PH-P2P-040 explicitly leaves stock receipting unchanged. Included deliberately: this group is downstream of a major programme, will see documents change format, and would otherwise hear nothing at all — which is how an unaffected team ends up convinced it has been forgotten.
impacts.benefit_narrative: Nothing changes in how you receipt stock — you'll just see a different PO reference format on the paperwork.
impacts.key_message: Your receipting process isn't changing. PO numbers will look different from January — that's all.
impacts.comms_channel: Team briefing; shift-handover note

impacts.as_is_process: Finance builds the goods-received-not-invoiced accrual from an ECC extract, adjusted by hand for the known lag in central goods receipting.
impacts.to_be_process: Same accrual process and same period-close calendar, sourced from the new system. The manual lag adjustment should reduce as receipting moves to the point of delivery, but the task itself is unchanged.
impacts.impacted_roles: Financial accountants running period close
impacts.impact_rationale: Low mechanical change — same task, new data source. Worth carrying in the register because the first period close after go-live is where receipting non-compliance (CI-006) will show up as an accrual variance, and Finance should be expecting it rather than investigating it.
impacts.benefit_narrative: The manual lag adjustment shrinks as receipting happens at the point of delivery rather than centrally in arrears.
impacts.key_message: Period close doesn't change. Expect a larger accrual variance in the first two closes while goods receipting beds in.
impacts.comms_channel: Finance team briefing; period-close checklist update
impacts.notes: Derived by inference from the goods receipt redesign rather than from a Finance interview — no period-close stakeholder has been spoken to. Validate with Financial Control.
